item.title: Officials urge Beaufort County residents to prepare for snow, high winds and extreme cold
item.description: Beaufort County officials warn of 8–12 inches of snow, high winds and days of subfreezing cold, urging residents to avoid travel, prepare for outages and check on neighbors.

item.title: Emergency Services Director urges residents to avoid unnecessary travel as heavy snow and high winds arrive today
item.description: Up to a foot of snow, subfreezing temps and high winds are set to bring whiteout conditions and dangerous roads to Beaufort County; officials urge no unnecessary travel after 12 p.m. today.

item.title: Washington set for swim championships after revised schedule
item.description: With the regionals scrapped due to the winter weather, the Washington High School swim team will turn its focus to the Class 4A state championship, scheduled for this Thursday.

item.title: Washington wrestling qualifies for Class 4A duals, will be on the road
item.description: Washington's wrestling team qualified for the postseason but will be on the road. The question now is whether they will wrestle on Tuesday.

item.title: The Academic Papers UK - A Better Way to Do Assignments in 2026
item.description: The UK academic standards are shifting, and students should adapt to their university guidelines in 2026 to succeed.

item.title: BCSO: Barricaded subject placed in custody
item.description: A barricaded subject was placed into custody today following a report of a domestic dispute, according to Beaufort County Sheriff's Office. On Monday, Feb. 2, at 11:02 a.m., deputies with Beaufort County Sheriff's Office and officers with Washington Police Department responded to a domestic disturbance at a residence in the 2000 block of West Fifth Street in Washington. item.title: Beaufort County sheriff gives update on road conditions
item.description: Winter weather doesn’t end when the snowfall stops. In fact, some of the most dangerous driving conditions appear after the snow has cleared, when roads look passable but remain unpredictable and hazardous. The North Carolina Department of Transportation continues to clear the roadways in Beaufort County. Primary roadways, such as US17, US264, and NC33 have greatly improved. item.title: Beaufort County faces days of icy roads and black ice after winter storm Gianna snowfall
item.description: Up to 14 inches of snow from Winter Storm Gianna will keep Beaufort County roads icy and dangerous all week as subfreezing temperatures prolong black ice and poor travel conditions.

item.title: Home deemed a total loss after six fire departments fight fire
item.description: Six fire departments battle blaze that destroys Belhaven waterfront home; snow hampers response as accidental fire linked to thawing frozen pipes.
